title: The Radiance of the Glory of God
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Jesus came in humility, but he is no longer weak. He reigns in heaven, and one day we will see him and thank him face to face.
exhortation: I just don't think enough about Jesus, his wonder and his majesty. This verse gives us a picture of him so glorious it's hard to wrap my mind around: the radiance of the glory of God, upholding the universe, reigning over angels.

I imagine the disciples had the same struggle. Jesus came in such humility, willingly taking on weakness, that we can forget he is no longer weak, frail and suffering. He is all-powerful and victorious, reigning in heaven. When he returns, Revelation says, he will strike down his enemies with a word. A word is all he needs.

When I ponder and meditate on this risen, powerful, glorious Jesus, I can't wait to see him: to finally see him with my own eyes, worship him, and thank him face to face for shedding his blood on the cross for my sin. We have a glorious future because we have a great and glorious Savior who will vanquish all our sin and all our enemies once and for all, and bring us into glory.
prayer: Jesus, you are the only one who could live perfectly the life no human being has ever lived from the beginning of creation to the end, the only wise King, the only one worthy. Your name is to be praised above every name, because you are the Lamb who was slain. Lord, do we understand even a tiny bit of the majesty and glory of what you have done for us?

May we think on it, ponder it and orient our lives around it. May we be fixed on you today, Lord Jesus, with every bit of our being. May every conversation we have, every post we make and every message we send be laced with the glory of God and wonder at who you are. All glory to you, Jesus.
